title: RiverCity Metro Rider Portal Accessibility Conformance Report

product:
  name: RiverCity Metro Rider Portal
  version: '2026.3'
  description: >-
    The public rider portal for RiverCity Metro Authority: trip planning,
    schedules, fares, service alerts, and pass-holder accounts.

author:
  name: Dana Okafor
  company_name: Meridian Digital Accessibility
  address: ''
  email: dana.okafor@meridian-a11y.example
  phone: ''
  website: https://meridian-a11y.example

vendor:
  name: Digital Services
  company_name: RiverCity Metro Authority
  address: ''
  email: digital@rivercitymetro.example
  phone: ''
  website: ''

release_date: '2026-07-28'

notes: >-
  Draft report. Serialized from the finished WCAG-EM 2.0 evaluation rcm-2026q3
  (evaluation window 2026-06-22 to 2026-07-28), commissioned by the RiverCity
  Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights. Conformance target: WCAG 2.2
  Level AA.

  Scope. Everything member-facing on rivercitymetro.org (trip planner,
  schedules, fares, service alerts, pass-holder account area), the RideRC
  native app ticket-activation flow, and the monthly PDF timetables.

  Named exclusion. The third-party real-time vehicle map iframe is excluded by
  the engagement letter: vendor-supplied, documented, and not remediable this
  cycle. No claim in this report covers it.

  Component scope. The web component is reported on every WCAG criterion and
  is backed by full coverage of the sample set. The electronic-docs and
  software components appear only on the criteria where evidence was actually
  collected: 1.3.1 for the PDF timetables, and 4.1.2 for the RideRC native app.
  Their absence from every other criterion is a coverage boundary, not a
  conformance claim. Neither surface was evaluated criterion by criterion, and
  both sit outside the web measurement stack. No authoring-tool surface is in
  scope. No hardware surface is in scope (fare validators belong to a separate
  procurement). No support-documentation surface was evaluated.

  Revised Section 508 chapters. This report uses the 508-edition catalog
  because the audit plan required that template, but the engagement was scoped
  and executed as a WCAG 2.2 AA evaluation. The functional performance
  criteria, hardware, software (502 to 504), and support documentation and
  services chapters are disabled because no evidence was collected for them.
  Until those chapters are completed, this document is a WCAG 2.2 AA
  conformance report in a Section 508 wrapper. It is not a Section 508
  conformance claim.

  Adherence and impact are orthogonal. The catalog adherence term records how
  much product functionality meets a criterion; it does not record how badly a
  person is blocked. Per-criterion notes carry the finding identifier,
  fingerprint, and severity from the evaluation record so that both readings
  survive into this report.

evaluation_methods_used: >-
  Methodology: WCAG-EM 2.0 (https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/). Evaluator:
  Meridian Digital Accessibility, reporting lead Dana Okafor. Evaluation window
  2026-06-22 to 2026-07-28. The base window closed 2026-07-24; a follow-up
  session on 2026-07-28 closed the one criterion still open at that point
  (3.1.2 Language of Parts).

  Sample set. Structured samples (11): S01 home, S02 trip planner, S03 route
  schedule, S04 service alerts, S05 fares, S06 account dashboard, S07 checkout
  steps 1 to 2, S08 contact and paratransit application form, S09 news article,
  S10 accessibility policy, S11 title-vi (2019 legacy info-page template).
  Random sample (1): R01 /riders/lost-and-found, drawn by seeded shuffle of the
  214-URL sitemap, seed 7391. Complete processes (2): P01 plan trip, buy
  monthly pass, confirmation (web; default and declined-payment error branches;
  traverses S02, S05, S07); P02 activate a purchased ticket in the RideRC
  native app (manual assistive-technology session, outside the web measurement
  stack). State coverage per web sample: default, loading, error, and expanded
  states where the template has them.

  Representativeness check. R01 surfaced the 2019 legacy info-page template,
  which was missing from the structured set, so S11 was added and evaluated.
  The second comparison surfaced no further content types or finding types.

  Accessibility-support baseline. NVDA 2026.1 with Firefox 141 on Windows 11;
  VoiceOver with Safari 18 on macOS 15; TalkBack 15 with Chrome on Android 15;
  and keyboard-only operation without a screen reader.

  Technologies relied upon. HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React), and WAI-ARIA. The
  RideRC app is native Kotlin/Swift and is not built on web technologies. The
  PDF timetables are PDF 1.7.

  Non-web evidence. Two manual sessions: the RideRC native app under TalkBack
  and VoiceOver on 2026-07-15, and a PDF document check on 2026-07-16.

legal_disclaimer: >-
  This report describes the conformance of the evaluated surfaces as of
  2026-07-28, on the basis of the sample set and accessibility-support baseline
  described under evaluation methods. It records a sampled evaluation, not an
  exhaustive test of every page, state, document, or device combination, and it
  is not a warranty. Claims apply only to the components and criteria recorded
  here; excluded and unevaluated surfaces are named in the notes and carry no
  claim. This draft has not been reviewed or adopted by the RiverCity Metro
  Authority.

related_documents:
  - url: https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/
    label: WCAG-EM 2.0, the evaluation methodology used for this engagement

license: ''

Reporting it as partially-supports would let a reader infer that most forms are fine.
